title: Tiered entitlement experiment: time-windowed add-ons and SLA activation playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Run a controlled experiment to evaluate a tiered add-on activation flow that combines longer observability retention, a compliance questionnaire 'pack', and a premium SLA as separately billable entitlements. The experiment tests (a) whether time-windowed activation (trial + graduated upsell) increases paid attachment rates vs immediate charge, (b) if gating the compliance pack behind a security questionnaire reduces legal review friction, and (c) acceptable revenue lift vs conversion tradeoffs for premium SLA. Deliver a playbook for rollout, UI mockups, gating logic, and a set of instrumentation queries for the console and billing systems.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document three activation flows: trial->conversion, direct purchase, and sales-assisted activation
Dashboardable metrics for conversion, attach-rate, churn-at-30/90 days, and MRR delta instrumented
Legal and Security questionnaire flow signed off by Marco Li (Legal) and Aisha Khan (Revenue Ops)
Billing integration (invoice line-items & usage tags) implemented for one pilot customer and validated end-to-end
Canary UI with feature flag and telemetry toggles deployed to 5% of new signups
tasks: Finalize pricing bands for observability retention tiers (30d / 90d / 365d) - PM + Revenue
Design questionnaire mapping to compliance pack entitlement (Design: DES-204)
Implement entitlement gating rules in backend (ENG-20104) and feature flagging
Add billing metadata for add-on line items and accounting tags (ENG-20678)
Create console CTA and flow for trial activation + auto-convert logic
Prepare contract addendum template for premium SLA customers
Run a pilot with two existing enterprise accounts (one PLG-led, one sales-led)
comments: 2026-02-26 — Sofia Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes attached. We agreed to measure both short-term attach rate and cohorted revenue impact over 90 days.
2026-03-02 — Evan Gupta: Decided to prefer a graduated trial (30d trial for observability retention to 90d paid tier) rather than free indefinite pilot; reduces churn noise in cohort analysis.
2026-03-04 — Aisha Khan: Recommend adding a telemetry credits experiment to offset perceived cost for PLG early adopters. Created sample credit model in spreadsheet.
2026-03-06 — Marco Li: Legal flagged the compliance questionnaire as high-touch if we allow self-attestation for SOC2 controls. Suggested two-tier questionnaire flow with evidence upload for tier-2.
2026-03-09 — Design review: Added a compact modal flow for quick accept/decline and an advanced flow for security teams. See attached Figma link.
2026-03-12 — Eng sync: Backend gating schema drafted; ENG-20104 will add entitlement flags and a 'grace period' TTL for staged activation. Estimate aligns with dependency.
2026-03-12 — PM note: Next steps are legal signoff on questionnaire, ledger tagging for billing, and wiring metrics to the dashboard (dashboard owner: Riley Cho).
notes: Tradeoffs discussed: aggressive pricing increases MRR per attach but reduces attach-rate among PLG signups. We will A/B two price points: conservative and aggressive.
Fallback policy: if billing tagging fails for pilot customers, we will fall back to manual invoicing and maintain 'pilot: true' metadata for reconciliation.
Success criteria (qualitative): Sales reports lower friction for contractual customers; Security reports reduced back-and-forth for small customers using questionnaire.
Contingency: if conversion lift < 6% after 60 days, halt rollouts and run customer interviews to identify friction points.
